newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek short money rates firm on FRN, bond funding.
newsitem.headline: Greek short money rates firm on FRN, bond funding.

text.p: Greek interbank depos in short dates up to a week firmed as players sought funding for FRNs and coupon bonds to be auctioned today. Market players said they expected average bids well above par on strong demand by institutionals.

"Shorts up to a week have firmed 20 basis points on auction-linked short covering by some players," a foreign bank dealer said. "The market is liquid and will remain so despite today's auction because of the large amount of expiries of state securities."
The finance ministry will auction three-year, 100 billion drachma bond that will feature a lower coupon at 10.70 percent from 11 percent previously.
The seven-year, 200 billion drachma FRN to be auctioned on Friday will also feature a lower base rate of 11.20 percent, down from 11.50 percent at the previous auction.
Bond dealers said there was strong demand for the FRNs and bonds by institutional investors who were loaded with cash.

"I think the primary reason for the success of today's auction is the institutionals' strong appetite for these securities that happens to be the last tax-free ones and expectations of a rate cut by the central bank," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Greece will impose a 7.5 percent on interest payments from securities issued effective January 1, 1997.

The central bank has kept its overnight bid unchanged at 12.40 percent for about three months and dealers have said they were bracing for a much awaited cut, perhaps sizeable, in the next couple of weeks or so.
Other dealers said they expected Greek banks with large branch networks to bid aggressively for the three-year coupon bond.
A roundup of a few dealers showed that they expected the average bid for the seven-year FRNs to range between 101.50-102 and the three-year coupon bonds to be aroundor above 100.50.
The mark was quoted at 158.95/05 drachmas from Tuesday's 159.200 fix, the dollar at 247.51/61 drachmas from 247.500 and the Ecu at 306.27/37 from 306.350 drachmas.
